items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: comedians like Roscoe Conklin Simmons, who was the son of the late Roscoe -- you remember, Roscoe Simmons the great orator? You've heard of him, haven't you?

ctx.x: He was from Washington, D. C. Claude Hopkins. Claud Hopkins, had a big band, he'd broadcast on the networks back in -- oh, back in the '30's. In the '30's, Orlando Robeson was a great singer with him. And made the "Trees" popular he used to sing that over and over -- and that used to come three or four afternoons a week out of New York. Anyway I met Claude Hopkins when he called himself the Six Gingersnaps, I thought perhaps you might've known them. That was back in 1927.

There was a Walker Theater there, which shows like Blanche Calloway, the sister of Cab Calloway, used to bring in shows there at the Walker Theater, that was -- that was dance teams, the dance team of Rector and Cooper, one of the greatest dance teams back in that era. And comedians like Roscoe Conklin Simmons, who was the son of the late Roscoe -- you remember, Roscoe Simmons the great orator? You've heard of him, haven't you?
